Last year, the Redox team received a grant to develop io_uring-like Ring Buffer support at the system task level, as a first step towards ring buffer communications between the application and the majority of system services. This phase of the work finished up in September, as the last pieces were put in place. [...] In addition to implementing the Ring Buffer machinery for our system services and drivers that can support it, an io_uring and liburing -like API for applications was completed and demonstrated. There was also substantial work done on support crates, including an async executor for drivers. And there was some very exciting work on various performance improvements, to allow much faster switching between applications and their system services. resumo: A team from the Research Institute of the McGill University Health Center (The Institute) have discovered a new type of extracellular vesicle released by migrating cancer cells, revealing a previously unknown way in which these cells shed their DNA as they move. The widespread and ongoing expansion of data centers will continue to gobble up enormous amounts of memory, while demand is expected to rise further as AI is incorporated into other industries like self-driving vehicles and robots. Why not produce more memory? Manufacturers are working on it, but it takes several years at minimum to build new semiconductor factories and spin up production to necessary levels. SK Hynix also points out that the actual manufacturing processes for increasingly advanced memory chips have gotten more technically challenging in recent years.
